title: AI delirium risk model compared prospectively with the 4AT screen in trauma patients
summary: In a prospective study of 2,002 trauma-ward patients, a previously developed random forest model applied to electronic health record data flagged 87.3% (165/189) of delirium cases as at risk, against 28.0% (5/189) for the 4AT score; it correctly classified 73.9% of non-delirium patients as not at risk versus 96.3% for the 4AT. The AUC was 0.884. Single ward, lower specificity than the 4AT, and no trial of effects on outcomes.
ai_technology: Previously developed random forest delirium risk model applied to electronic health record data

evidence.tested: Prospective head-to-head comparison of a previously developed model with the 4AT score in 2,002 trauma-ward patients.
evidence.unknown: Effect on patient outcomes or workflow; performance in other settings; model development was not part of this study; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest model predicted delirium risk from routine health record data.
